gallery.filename: Disused Newry canal, Scarva (1) - geograph.org.uk - 175517.jpg
gallery.title: File:Disused Newry canal, Scarva (1) - geograph.org.uk - 175517.jpg
gallery.description: Disused Newry canal, Scarva (1). The Newry canal connected Lough Neagh (via the River Bann) to the town of Newry and then through the Newry ship canal to Carlingford Lough and the Irish Sea. The canal opened in 1742, had become largely derelict by 1939 and was formally abandoned in 1949. This is the canal at Scarva (looking towards Newry).  It is now overgrown for most of its length. The tow path has been restored for walkers and cyclists.  See also 262586.
